title: Color Order · Together
hook: Find a game, gather your friends and start playing.

knows: The group wants an activity to play together.
doesNotKnow: The setup, turn and ending for this house-rule format.

misconception: The group has to know a complicated rulebook before starting.
objective: Learn how to play Color Order · Together with friends.

claims.text: Original house rules: Arrange three colored papers in a row and cover them after a brief look. The lead names the colors in order. The colors are named in their original order. Play eight turns in total, rotating the lead. The group wins together if at least five turns succeed.
claims.source: Original playable house-rule proposal; not an authoritative ruleset for a traditional game.

claims.text: For this version: 2–8 players; materials: Three different colored papers and a cloth.
claims.source: Proposed setup and player range for this activity.

recall.question: In Color Order, what counts as a successful turn?
options: The group ends the round before anyone plays.
The colors are named in their original order.
The lead skips the turn without attempting it.
recall.why: The colors are named in their original order.

game.materials: Three different colored papers and a cloth
